brief.headline: Fix the 40% return problem first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80 on volume—and line up Manjushree as second source

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80/piece for caps at higher volumes or looser specs
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc); verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec—we want that headroom

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 days—no reason to pay earlier until quality stabilizes

brief.financialLeverage: Scorpion publishes no financial statements, so we don't know their revenue, profit, or cash position. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is tiny—we're not a major customer. With 40% of their deliveries getting sent back, they need us more for steady volume than we need them for supply. Push firmly on price and quality, and use the backup pipeline (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) to show we can walk if they don't fix both.

evidence.point: 40% of their deliveries are reversed or returned—a serious quality or paperwork issue
Our annual spend with them is just ₹1.66 L—we're a small customer
Market asking price for 28 mm PP caps runs ₹0.55–1.20/piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95
Market verdict says modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec
We currently pay them 30 days after receipt—not the worst terms in our book

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)—pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100)—pails, containers, pharma packaging; strong and profitable alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)—pan-India manufacturer; medium-confidence match for rigid plastics

risks: 40% return rate means every order risks disruption—lock in a quality-fix plan with dates before committing more volume
No public financials—we can't see if they're stable or struggling; de-risk by qualifying Manjushree or Mold-Tek now
Our ₹1.66 L spend is tiny to them (if they're any size at all)—they may not prioritize fixes or price cuts for us
If we push too hard on price before quality improves, returns will eat any saving—fix defects first, then negotiate price
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to grow this relationship, but 40% of your deliveries come back—let's agree on a quality plan today, and then talk about hitting ₹0.65–0.80 per cap at scale.
